# Part I. Illumina BioInsight: Product portfolio overview

**Illumina BioInsight** is Illumina's business division focusing on biological data, bioinformatics software, data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI). Its objective is to provide an end-to-end informatics ecosystem that transforms sequencing data into biological and clinical insights.

Illumina launched its unified **BioInsight Platform in October 2026**, bringing together its previously separate informatics products under a common software environment, account and subscription model ([launch announcement](https://www.illumina.com/company/news-center/press-releases/2026/29256.html)).

The important distinction is that these products are not all designed for the same type or stage of analysis. Some process raw sequencing data, some perform downstream biological analysis, some interpret genetic variants, and others provide the underlying computational infrastructure.

```{=html}
<div class="node gray" style="margin-top:12px"><strong>BioInsight Platform Core (formerly ICA)</strong><small>Cloud computing · Data storage · Pipeline execution · APIs · Data management<br>Shared infrastructure supporting the applications above</small></div>
<div class="figcap">Conceptual workflow based on Illumina's product portfolio. The arrows represent typical data flow rather than mandatory dependencies between products.</div></div>
```

## 2. Summary table of BioInsight products

| Product | Main purpose | Typical input | Typical output |
|---|---|---|---|
| [BaseSpace Sequence Hub (BSSH)](https://sapac.illumina.com/products/by-type/informatics-products/basespace-sequence-hub.html) | Sequencing run monitoring, data management and analysis apps | Sequencing run data, FASTQ | Run QC, FASTQ, app-specific results |
| [DRAGEN](https://www.illumina.com/products/by-type/informatics-products/dragen-bio-it-platform.html) | High-performance secondary analysis | BCL, FASTQ, BAM | BAM, CRAM, VCF, count matrices |
| [Connected Multiomics (ICM)](https://sapac.illumina.com/products/by-type/informatics-products/connected-multiomics.html) | Downstream biological analysis and multiomics integration | Expression matrices, spatial data, proteomic data | Clusters, DEGs, pathways, cell types, visualizations |
| [Emedgene](https://sapac.illumina.com/products/by-type/informatics-products/emedgene.html) | Germline variant interpretation | Genetic variants, phenotype, family information | Prioritized variants, pathogenicity evidence, research reports |
| [Connected Insights (ICI)](https://sapac.illumina.com/products/by-type/informatics-products/connected-insights.html) | Somatic variant interpretation for oncology | VCF, cancer type, genomic biomarkers | Variant interpretation, therapy evidence, clinical trial matching |
| [BioInsight Platform Core (formerly ICA)](https://sapac.illumina.com/products/by-type/informatics-products/connected-analytics.html) | Cloud infrastructure and customized bioinformatics pipelines | Raw or processed genomic data, workflow definitions | Pipeline results, managed datasets |
| BioInsight Data | Curated biological datasets and research evidence | Public and proprietary datasets | Harmonized datasets, reference cohorts |
| [Clarity LIMS](https://www.illumina.com/products/by-type/informatics-products/lab-management-software/clarity-lims.html) | Laboratory information management | Sample information, laboratory metadata | Sample tracking, workflow records |
| [Correlation Engine](https://supportassets.illumina.com/products/by-type/informatics-products/connected-analytics/modules/correlation-engine.html) | Public multiomics data mining and biological interpretation | Gene lists, molecular signatures | Disease associations, related studies, biological evidence |
| [Partek Flow](https://sapac.illumina.com/products/by-type/informatics-products/partek-flow.html) | Graphical bioinformatics analysis | FASTQ, expression matrices, spatial data | Analysis workflows, statistical results, plots |

Source: [Illumina software portfolio](https://sapac.illumina.com/products/by-type/informatics-products.html) and individual product documentation.

## 3. What does each product actually do?

### 3.1 BaseSpace Sequence Hub (BSSH)

*Sequencing data management and analysis portal*

BaseSpace is primarily the interface connecting sequencing instruments, sequencing data and ready-to-use bioinformatics applications.

- Monitor sequencing runs remotely.
- Review sequencing QC metrics, such as Q30 and yield.
- Store, download and share sequencing data.
- Launch preconfigured bioinformatics applications.
- Manage sequencing projects and analysis results.

```{=html}
<div class="diagram lane"><div class="node"><strong>NovaSeq X Plus</strong><small>Sequencing run</small></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="node"><strong>BaseSpace</strong><small>Data and run QC</small></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="node"><strong>Analysis apps</strong><small>Results</small></div></div>
```

**Simple understanding:** BaseSpace is a sequencing data portal with an application store for running bioinformatics analyses.

### 3.2 DRAGEN (Dynamic Read Analysis for GENomics)

*High-performance secondary analysis engine*

DRAGEN is the computational engine that processes sequencing reads and converts them into meaningful molecular measurements. It supports applications including:

- Whole-genome and whole-exome sequencing.
- Germline and somatic variant calling.
- RNA-seq alignment and gene quantification.
- Structural variant and copy number variant detection.
- Methylation, single-cell and spatial analysis for supported assays.

```{=html}
<div class="diagram"><div class="node gray">Raw sequencing reads (FASTQ)</div><div class="arrow">↓</div><div class="node blue"><strong>DRAGEN</strong><small>Alignment → Quantification / Variant calling</small></div><div class="arrow">↓</div><div class="lane"><div class="node"><strong>BAM / CRAM</strong><small>Alignment</small></div><div class="node"><strong>VCF</strong><small>Genetic variants</small></div><div class="node"><strong>Count matrix</strong><small>Gene expression</small></div></div></div>
```

DRAGEN was originally particularly associated with FPGA hardware acceleration. DRAGEN v4.6 also expands deployment to supported standard CPU and cloud environments ([launch announcement](https://www.illumina.com/company/news-center/press-releases/2026/29256.html)).

**Simple understanding:** DRAGEN performs functions comparable to combinations of BWA, STAR, GATK, featureCounts and other secondary analysis tools, depending on the selected workflow.

### 3.3 Illumina Connected Multiomics (ICM)

*Downstream biological discovery and multiomics analysis*

This is the product most relevant to researchers performing transcriptomics, single-cell and spatial data analysis.

Unlike DRAGEN, which primarily generates molecular measurements, Connected Multiomics focuses on identifying biological patterns, comparing experimental groups and interpreting results.

Illumina also provides biological contextualization through curated public datasets and research evidence. Its spatial functionality includes overlaying expression data on tissue images, interactive filtering, differential expression and cell typing ([product page](https://sapac.illumina.com/products/by-type/informatics-products/connected-multiomics.html)).

**Simple understanding:** Connected Multiomics is a cloud-based graphical biological data analysis environment, broadly comparable in purpose to Partek Flow and downstream analysis with Seurat or Scanpy.

### 3.4 Emedgene

*AI-assisted germline variant interpretation*

Emedgene focuses on identifying potentially disease-causing inherited genetic variants, particularly for rare genetic disease research.

Its functionality includes variant annotation, phenotype-based prioritization, inheritance analysis, pathogenicity evidence assessment and report preparation.

```{=html}
<div class="diagram"><div class="lane"><div class="node gray"><strong>VCF</strong><small>Genetic variants</small></div><div class="node gray"><strong>HPO terms</strong><small>Patient phenotype</small></div><div class="node gray"><strong>Pedigree</strong><small>Family information</small></div></div><div class="arrow">↓</div><div class="node purple"><strong>Emedgene</strong><small>Annotation · AI prioritization · Evidence curation</small></div><div class="arrow">↓</div><div class="node"><strong>Illustrative prioritized variant report</strong><table class="table"><thead><tr><th>Gene</th><th>Candidate variant</th><th>Evidence</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>BRCA2</td><td>Variant A</td><td>Pathogenic</td></tr><tr><td>BRCA1</td><td>Variant B</td><td>Likely pathogenic</td></tr><tr><td>PALB2</td><td>Variant C</td><td>VUS</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
```

For example, a whole-genome sequencing dataset may contain millions of genetic variants. Emedgene helps researchers narrow these down to candidates that may explain a patient's phenotype.

**Simple understanding:** DRAGEN tells you which genetic variants are present; Emedgene helps you understand which inherited variants may be responsible for a disease.

### 3.5 Illumina Connected Insights (ICI)

*Somatic variant interpretation and precision oncology*

Connected Insights is mainly designed for oncology genomic interpretation rather than gene expression analysis. It helps researchers connect tumor mutations and genomic biomarkers with scientific literature, treatment evidence, guidelines and clinical trials.

```{=html}
<div class="diagram"><div class="node gray"><strong>Tumor sequencing results</strong><small>Somatic VCF · Cancer type · TMB · MSI · HRD</small></div><div class="arrow">↓</div><div class="node orange"><strong>Connected Insights</strong><small>Variant annotation and oncology evidence matching</small></div><div class="arrow">↓</div><div class="lane"><div class="node"><strong>Biomarkers</strong><small>Variant significance</small></div><div class="node"><strong>Therapies</strong><small>Treatment evidence</small></div><div class="node"><strong>Clinical trials</strong><small>Trial matching</small></div></div></div>
```

**Simple understanding:** Connected Insights helps answer what a particular tumor mutation means and what potential therapeutic evidence exists for it.

### 3.6 BioInsight Platform Core — formerly Illumina Connected Analytics (ICA)

*Cloud infrastructure and bioinformatics workflow execution*

ICA has been renamed **BioInsight Platform Core** as part of the new platform. It provides the infrastructure for:

- Cloud data storage and management.
- Large-scale bioinformatics pipeline execution.
- Customized workflows and containerized applications.
- API-based automation and integration.
- Data sharing, access control and provenance tracking.
- Running DRAGEN and other supported analysis pipelines.

```{=html}
<div class="diagram"><div class="lane"><div class="node">DRAGEN</div><div class="node">Emedgene</div><div class="node">Connected Insights</div></div><div class="lane" style="margin-top:8px"><div class="node">Connected Multiomics</div><div class="node">BaseSpace</div><div class="node">Custom pipelines</div></div><div class="arrow">↕</div><div class="node blue"><strong>BioInsight Platform Core</strong><div class="lane" style="margin-top:10px"><div class="node blue">Compute</div><div class="node blue">Storage</div><div class="node blue">Workflows</div></div></div></div>
```

**Simple understanding:** BioInsight Platform Core is similar in purpose to a cloud-based bioinformatics computing platform, rather than a specific analysis algorithm. Its role is broadly comparable to platforms such as Seqera Platform or an institutional HPC environment with workflow management capabilities ([Platform Core](https://www.illumina.com/products/by-type/informatics-products/connected-analytics.html)).

### 3.7 BioInsight Data and BioInsight AI Lab

These represent the expansion of Illumina beyond sequencing and conventional bioinformatics software.

| Component | Main function |
|---|---|
| BioInsight Data | Harmonizes and annotates public and proprietary biological datasets for reuse |
| Correlation Engine | Searches and compares molecular signatures against curated public studies |
| BioInsight AI Lab | Develops genomic AI models for biological interpretation |
| SpliceAI / SpliceAI2 | Predicts the effects of genetic variants on RNA splicing |
| Billion Cell Atlas | Large-scale cellular data resource initiative supporting drug discovery |
| Alliance for Genomic Discovery | Large-scale human genome data resource for genomic discovery |

The aim is to combine a researcher's own data with existing biological knowledge and AI predictions, rather than analyzing every dataset in isolation.

## 4. Emedgene vs Connected Insights vs Connected Multiomics

These three products are mainly positioned at the tertiary analysis and biological interpretation stage, but address very different research questions.

| Feature | Emedgene | Connected Insights | Connected Multiomics |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main application | Inherited genetic diseases | Precision oncology | Biological discovery |
| Analysis target | Germline variants | Somatic variants | Molecular expression and profiles |
| Main data | DNA variants | Tumor DNA variants and biomarkers | RNA, DNA, proteins, epigenomic profiles |
| Typical analysis | Variant prioritization | Variant actionability | Statistical and biological analysis |
| AI application | Pathogenic variant prioritization | Evidence matching and interpretation | Biological interpretation |
| Main results | Candidate disease-causing variants | Biomarker and therapy evidence | DEGs, cell types, pathways, clusters |
| Typical users | Geneticists | Oncology researchers | Biologists and bioinformaticians |
| Example question | Which BRCA2 variant may cause inherited cancer susceptibility? | Which therapies are associated with a tumor's EGFR mutation? | Which immune cell populations differ between cancer patients and healthy controls? |

## 5. Connected Multiomics vs Partek Flow

This is particularly relevant to the CPOS Bioinformatics Core, considering the existing on-premises Partek Flow service.

Illumina positions Partek Flow as its standalone, on-premises multiomics analysis option and Connected Multiomics as its integrated cloud-based solution.

| Feature | Partek Flow | Connected Multiomics |
|---|---|---|
| Abbreviation | PF | ICM |
| Deployment | On-premises option | Cloud-based |
| Infrastructure | Institution-managed server | BioInsight Platform Core |
| User interface | Graphical | Graphical |
| Bulk RNA-seq | Supported | Supported |
| scRNA-seq | Supported | Supported |
| Spatial transcriptomics | Supported | Supported |
| Proteomics | Workflow-dependent | Supported |
| Secondary analysis | Built-in workflows | Primarily integrated with DRAGEN or imported results |
| Third-party data | Supported | Supported |
| Computational scalability | Depends on local resources | Elastic cloud resources |
| Data management | Local infrastructure | Cloud infrastructure |
| Integration with Illumina products | Available | Native ecosystem integration |

### Can Connected Multiomics analyze 10x Genomics data?

**Yes.** Illumina states that Connected Multiomics supports matrices generated by third-party analysis tools, including Seurat, Scanpy, Cell Ranger and Space Ranger.

```{=html}
<div class="diagram"><div class="lane"><div class="node"><strong>DRAGEN</strong><small>Illumina workflows</small></div><div class="node"><strong>Cell Ranger</strong><small>10x single-cell</small></div><div class="node"><strong>Space Ranger</strong><small>10x spatial</small></div></div><div class="arrow">↓</div><div class="node gray"><strong>Secondary analysis outputs</strong><small>Count matrices · Metadata · Spatial information</small></div><div class="arrow">↓</div><div class="node green"><strong>Illumina Connected Multiomics</strong><small>Downstream analysis and visualization</small></div><div class="arrow">↓</div><div class="lane"><div class="node">Cell typing</div><div class="node">Differential expression</div><div class="node">Biological interpretation</div></div></div>
```

Relevant documentation:

- [Supported data types](https://help.multiomics.illumina.com/icm/reference/supported-data-types)
- [Data input and upload](https://help.multiomics.illumina.com/icm/introduction/upload-data-files)
- [Connected Multiomics release notes](https://help.multiomics.illumina.com/icm/reference/software-release-notes)

However, this does not mean that all Partek Flow functions are available in Connected Multiomics. Exact algorithm availability, Visium HD bin-size support, import requirements and multi-sample spatial analysis capabilities should be evaluated separately.

## 6. Which products are relevant to a Bioinformatics Core?

Considering the existing sequencing pipelines, HPC infrastructure and Partek Flow service, the products can be prioritized as follows.

| Product | Relevance | Potential application at CPOS |
|---|---|---|
| Connected Multiomics | Very high | Cloud-based single-cell, spatial and multiomics analysis service |
| DRAGEN | Very high | Standardized secondary analysis pipelines |
| BioInsight Platform Core | High | Cloud computing, pipeline automation and scalability |
| BaseSpace | High | Sequencing run monitoring and data delivery |
| Partek Flow | High | Existing on-premises analysis service |
| Clarity LIMS | Medium–high | Sample and laboratory workflow management |
| Correlation Engine | Medium | Biological interpretation and public data mining |
| Emedgene | Application-specific | Germline variant interpretation service |
| Connected Insights | Application-specific | Oncology genomic interpretation service |
| BioInsight Data | Application-specific | Large-scale cohort analysis and research discovery |

Illumina advertises a 30-day BioInsight Platform trial, including 100 BioInsight Credits and 1 TB of storage. Its new commercial model emphasizes usage-based credits ([pricing details](https://sapac.illumina.com/products/by-type/informatics-products/bioinsight-platform/pricing/pricing-details.html)).

For the core facility, investigate whether Connected Multiomics could complement or eventually replace parts of the existing Partek Flow service. The key evaluation criteria would be functionality, computational performance, cloud costs, data privacy, third-party assay compatibility and workflow reproducibility.

## 7. Summary — an easy way to remember

| Product | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| Clarity LIMS | Where are my samples? |
| BaseSpace | How is my sequencing run performing? |
| DRAGEN | What variants or molecular measurements are present? |
| Connected Multiomics | What biological differences exist between my samples? |
| Emedgene | Which inherited variant may cause disease? |
| Connected Insights | What is the significance of this tumor mutation? |
| BioInsight Data | What existing biological data can support my findings? |
| BioInsight Platform Core | Where are my data stored and my pipelines executed? |

In short, Illumina is moving from being primarily a sequencing technology provider towards providing an integrated **sequencing + bioinformatics + cloud computing + biological data + AI ecosystem**.

The product classification and workflow diagrams above are a synthesis of Illumina's official documentation, rather than an official product architecture diagram. The assessment is based on publicly available documentation, not hands-on testing of the new platform.

# Part II. Illumina StrataMap Spatial Transcriptome

**StrataMap is Illumina's own sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics technology**, officially launched on June 8, 2026. It was previously known as the Illumina Spatial Solution ([launch announcement](https://www.illumina.com/company/news-center/press-releases/2026/582e652d-8a03-475c-87da-db84a18b0b1a.html)).

It is a direct competitor to **10x Genomics Visium HD**, enabling researchers to measure genome-wide gene expression while preserving the spatial location of transcripts within tissue sections.

Unlike Connected Multiomics, StrataMap is not simply bioinformatics software. It is an end-to-end solution covering tissue preparation, spatial RNA capture, library preparation, sequencing and bioinformatics analysis.

## 1. Main features

```{=html}
<div class="diagram visual-grid"><div class="node"><small>Spatial feature resolution</small><div class="metric">1 µm</div><small>Subcellular-scale capture features</small></div><div class="node"><small>Total capture area</small><div class="metric">7.5 cm²</div><small>Large tissue coverage</small></div><div class="node"><small>Gene coverage</small><div class="metric">Whole transcriptome</div><small>Poly(A)-based RNA capture</small></div><div class="node"><small>Sample-to-result time</small><div class="metric">&lt; 5 days</div><small>Manufacturer-reported workflow</small></div></div>
```

| Feature | StrataMap |
|---|---|
| Technology | Sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics |
| RNA capture | Poly(A) capture |
| Sample type | Fresh frozen tissue |
| FFPE | Under development; initial customer enablement targeted for 2027 |
| Species | Broadly compatible with eukaryotic species |
| Gene panel | No predefined gene panel required |
| Tissue imaging | H&E staining and brightfield imaging |
| Sequencing | Illumina sequencing platforms |
| Secondary analysis | DRAGEN StrataMap |
| Tertiary analysis | Connected Multiomics |
| Additional specialized instrument | Not required, provided existing imaging equipment meets specifications |

Sources: [Illumina official product information](https://www.illumina.com/products/by-type/sequencing-kits/library-prep-kits/stratamap-spatial.html) and launch announcement.

## 2. How does StrataMap work?

The underlying principle is similar to Visium HD 3′: capture RNA using spatially barcoded oligonucleotides, sequence the captured RNA, and reconstruct its original location within the tissue.

## 3. StrataMap vs Visium HD vs Xenium

| Feature | Illumina StrataMap | Visium HD 3′ | Visium HD | Xenium |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Company | Illumina | 10x Genomics | 10x Genomics | 10x Genomics |
| Technology | Sequencing | Sequencing | Sequencing | Imaging |
| Capture method | Poly(A) | Poly(A) | Probe-based | Probe-based |
| Resolution | 1 µm features | 2 µm squares | 2 µm squares | Subcellular |
| Gene coverage | Unbiased transcriptome | Unbiased transcriptome | Transcriptome-wide probe set | Targeted panel |
| Species | Broad eukaryotic | Broad, reference-dependent | Probe-dependent | Probe-dependent |
| Fresh frozen | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| FFPE | In development | No | Yes | Yes |
| Capture area | 17 × 15 or 50 × 15 mm | 6.5 × 6.5 mm | 6.5 × 6.5 or 11 × 11 mm | Assay-dependent |
| Specialized instrument | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Secondary analysis | DRAGEN StrataMap | Space Ranger | Space Ranger | Xenium Onboard Analysis |
| Downstream analysis | Connected Multiomics | Loupe, Seurat, etc. | Loupe, Seurat, etc. | Xenium Explorer, Seurat, etc. |

Sources: [StrataMap](https://www.illumina.com/products/by-brand/stratamap.html), [Visium HD](https://www.10xgenomics.com/platforms/visium), [Xenium](https://www.10xgenomics.com/platforms/xenium). Specifications depend on assay version.

### Capture area comparison

```{=html}
<div class="diagram"><svg viewBox="0 0 340 218" style="width:100%;max-width:680px;display:block;margin:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="20" y="13" width="300" height="90" rx="2" fill="#487EBA" fill-opacity=".23" stroke="#487EBA" stroke-width="1.5"/><g fill="#20344c" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif"><text x="170" y="46" font-size="13" font-weight="600">StrataMap Large</text><text x="170" y="65" font-size="12">50 × 15 mm</text><text x="170" y="83" font-size="11">750 mm²</text><rect x="20" y="120" width="102" height="90" rx="2" fill="#487EBA" fill-opacity=".23" stroke="#487EBA"/><text x="71" y="151" font-size="11" font-weight="600">StrataMap S</text><text x="71" y="167" font-size="10">17 × 15 mm</text><text x="71" y="183" font-size="10">255 mm²</text><rect x="145" y="120" width="66" height="66" rx="2" fill="#40A78A" fill-opacity=".25" stroke="#40A78A"/><text x="178" y="141" font-size="10" font-weight="600">Visium HD</text><text x="178" y="156" font-size="9">11 × 11 mm</text><text x="178" y="171" font-size="10">121 mm²</text><rect x="259" y="120" width="39" height="39" rx="2" fill="#40A78A" fill-opacity=".25" stroke="#40A78A"/><text x="278" y="175" font-size="10" font-weight="600">Visium HD</text><text x="278" y="189" font-size="10">6.5 × 6.5 mm</text><text x="278" y="203" font-size="10">42.25 mm²</text></g></svg><div class="figcap">Capture areas drawn to the same scale. Visium values represent one capture area rather than an entire slide.</div><hr><div class="metric">17.8× larger</div>StrataMap Large compared with a single standard 6.5 mm Visium HD capture area.</div>
```

One important distinction: **1 µm capture resolution does not automatically mean better single-cell gene expression sensitivity.** Actual biological resolution also depends on RNA diffusion, capture efficiency, sequencing depth, binning and cell segmentation. Independent benchmarking would be needed to establish superiority.

## 4. How StrataMap fits into the BioInsight ecosystem

You can directly compare Illumina's end-to-end workflow with the existing 10x Genomics workflow.

```{=html}
<div class="diagram"><div class="lane"><div class="node blue"><strong>Illumina</strong></div><div class="node green"><strong>10x Genomics</strong></div></div><div class="figcap" style="text-align:center;margin:9px 0 5px">Spatial assay</div><div class="lane"><div class="node blue"><strong>StrataMap</strong></div><div class="node green"><strong>Visium HD</strong></div></div><div class="lane"><div class="arrow" style="flex:1">↓</div><div class="arrow" style="flex:1">↓</div></div><div class="figcap" style="text-align:center;margin:9px 0 5px">Sequencing</div><div class="lane"><div class="node blue"><strong>Illumina NovaSeq X</strong></div><div class="node green"><strong>Illumina NovaSeq X</strong></div></div><div class="lane"><div class="arrow" style="flex:1">↓</div><div class="arrow" style="flex:1">↓</div></div><div class="figcap" style="text-align:center;margin:9px 0 5px">Secondary analysis</div><div class="lane"><div class="node blue"><strong>DRAGEN StrataMap</strong></div><div class="node green"><strong>Space Ranger</strong></div></div><div class="lane"><div class="arrow" style="flex:1">↓</div><div class="arrow" style="flex:1">↓</div></div><div class="figcap" style="text-align:center;margin:9px 0 5px">Processed data</div><div class="lane"><div class="node blue"><strong>Spatial expression matrix</strong></div><div class="node green"><strong>Spatial expression matrix</strong></div></div><div class="lane"><div class="arrow" style="flex:1">↓</div><div class="arrow" style="flex:1">↓</div></div><div class="figcap" style="text-align:center;margin:9px 0 5px">Downstream analysis</div><div class="lane"><div class="node blue"><strong>Connected Multiomics</strong></div><div class="node green"><strong>Seurat / Partek Flow / Loupe</strong></div></div></div>
```

Therefore, the Illumina products have different responsibilities:

| Product | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| StrataMap | Generate spatial transcriptomics libraries |
| DRAGEN StrataMap | Convert sequencing data into spatial gene expression data |
| Connected Multiomics | Perform downstream biological analysis and visualization |
| BioInsight Platform Core | Provide cloud computing and data management infrastructure |
| BaseSpace | Sequencing run management and analysis initiation |

## 5. Potential benefits for CPOS

Considering the existing NovaSeq X Plus infrastructure and spatial transcriptomics analysis services, StrataMap is worth investigating for several reasons:

- **Lower instrument investment:** No dedicated spatial instrument is required beyond compatible existing equipment.
- **Larger tissue coverage:** Suitable for large tissue sections and multiple tissue samples on one slide.
- **Non-model organisms:** Poly(A)-based capture avoids dependence on species-specific probe panels.
- **Integrated bioinformatics:** Illumina provides both secondary and tertiary analysis software.
- **Potential new core service:** A complementary spatial transcriptomics service alongside Visium HD.

Before introducing the service, evaluate sequencing requirements, cost per sample, DRAGEN output formats, compatibility with Seurat and Scanpy, cloud computing costs, and sensitivity at equivalent sequencing depth.

This assessment is based on published product specifications, not independent experimental benchmarking.
